court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: I Additional Family Court Judge, Chennai (FCOP Nos. 440 of 2005 and 910 of 2006)
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1999. The husband filed for divorce under FCOP No. 440 of 2005, while the wife sought restitution of conjugal rights under FCOP No. 910 of 2006. The trial court granted a decree of divorce to the husband and dismissed the wife's petition.

legal_principles.principle: The conduct of the parties can affect the normal marital life.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court observed that the conduct of the appellant had affected the normal marital life and inspite of persuasion by the respondent, she did not change her behavioural pattern.
cited_cases: Meenakshi vs Premkumar Nachiappan on 29 January, 2019

legal_principles.principle: Matrimonial cruelty can be inferred from the conduct of the parties.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court further held that the relationship between the appellant and the respondent was not normal and cordial and that the respondent was subjected to matrimonial cruelty by the appellant.
cited_cases: Meenakshi vs Premkumar Nachiappan on 29 January, 2019

outcome.final_order: The final order is not specified in this excerpt, but it appears that the appeal was allowed.
